$comment: The curated input to corpus/pin.mjs: every source it fetches, the nodes the map names, the map's headers and the edges between them. Relations and bases are written by hand from each project's own public text, read 2026-09-22; the edges that name a header restate earlier ones from their pinned bytes alone, read 2026-09-23. map writes map/header.yaml, and each entry of headers writes a later header. An edge that names a header belongs to it; replaces names the edge or header it restates, which stays as it was signed. corpus/manifest.json records what each location served when it was fetched.
subject: typedstandards.org

map.title: Typed Standards: relations to public projects
comment: map.yaml: Typed Standards' technical relations to public projects, in three rings.
After this comment, one header document, then one YAML document per edge. Outside x-typedstandards,
each edge uses only the field names the SciOS core-and-satellite examples show for an edge
(id, createdAt, subject, object). Every other field is under x-typedstandards.
Written by corpus/pin.mjs from corpus/sources.json and corpus/manifest.json. This file's exact bytes
are the output of one signed Typed Standards record in package/.
map.edgeTypes: The published schema shows one edge type, orbits, from a satellite to a core. This map has no orbits edge. No core record exists in this domain to be the object of one, and the model says a core is never a satellite. Each edge names its relation in x-typedstandards.relation, because the published schema has no edge type for any of these relations.

relations.builds-on: The subject implements, or normatively uses, the object's published specification or code.
relations.complements: The two address different layers or artifact classes of one job and can be used together. Neither depends on the other.
relations.could-emit: The subject's own public text states an intent to produce Typed Standards records, cited by URL and date.
relations.adjacent: A related problem space. Neither depends on the other, and there is no public statement of an intent to emit or evaluate Typed Standards records.

rings.3: Implementations, possible emitters, and agent runtimes.

map.refs: Each ref is either a file at a 40-character commit SHA, a dated W3C TR URL, an rfc-editor.org text URL, or a published npm release tarball. A ref gives both the location and the SHA-256 of the bytes that location served when it was fetched. Where a project has no immutable location, the ref gives the location, a null sha256, and the reason in x-typedstandards.pin.

dropped.name: DSSE (Dead Simple Signing Envelope)
dropped.reason: Typed Standards uses neither the DSSE envelope nor its pre-authentication encoding. It signs an Ed25519ph signature over the envelope-hash hex string (specification §8.3.1). The specification does name DSSE: its adjacent-standards table lists in-toto / DSSE (§5.5), and Appendix C lists DSSE as a candidate envelope-serialization profile for in-toto-native consumers. Nothing is built on it. The in-toto entry covers the conventions the specification does use.

edges.name: W3C PROV-O
edges.subject: typedstandards.org
edges.basis: Every record's provenance graph is PROV-O JSON-LD, and the envelope does not redefine derivation, attribution or generation (specification §5.5, §8.1.4).

edges.name: in-toto Attestation Framework (DigestSet)
edges.subject: typedstandards.org
edges.basis: The contentHash field uses the in-toto DigestSet convention (algorithm name to hex digest), and the type URIs follow the pattern of in-toto's predicateType (specification §5.5).

curation.reason: Kept for in-toto. DSSE, listed beside it, is dropped (see the header).

edges.name: Sigstore Rekor (hashedrekord)
edges.subject: typedstandards.org
edges.basis: Records submit hashedrekord entries, and verify-core checks Merkle inclusion against a pinned Rekor log key (specification §8.3.2, §9.2 check #8). This example's records carry no Rekor entry.

edges.name: RFC 3161 Time-Stamp Protocol
edges.subject: typedstandards.org
edges.basis: Records carry RFC 3161 timestamp tokens, which verify-core checks against pinned TSA anchors (specification §9.2 check #7). This example's records carry none.

edges.name: RFC 8785 JSON Canonicalization Scheme
edges.subject: typedstandards.org
edges.basis: The envelope hash is the SHA-256 of the RFC 8785 canonicalization of the unsigned envelope (specification §8.2).

edges.name: RFC 8032 EdDSA (Ed25519ph)
edges.subject: typedstandards.org
edges.basis: Every record signature is Ed25519ph, defined in RFC 8032 §5.1 (specification §8.3.1).

curation.reason: The signature algorithm of every record, this example's two included.

edges.name: The did:key Method v0.9
edges.subject: typedstandards.org
edges.basis: A self-certifying signer's identifier is a did:key in base58btc form, derived from the signing key (specification §8.5.1, hub ADR-0030). This example's two records use one.

edges.name: Discourse Graphs
edges.subject: typedstandards.org
edges.basis: The specification takes its claim, question and evidence content types and its support, opposition and answer relations from the Discourse Graphs pattern (§5.5, §7.5). Those content types are specified, not built, and the current schema file names its relations differently.

edges.name: C2PA Technical Specification 2.3
edges.publisher: Coalition for Content Provenance and Authenticity
edges.subject: typedstandards.org
edges.basis: C2PA binds signed provenance manifests to media assets, and Typed Standards signs production records for analytical artifacts. It is the same job for a different artifact class, and neither depends on the other (specification §5.5).

edges.name: W3C Verifiable Credentials Data Model v2.0
edges.subject: typedstandards.org
edges.basis: A data model for issuer-secured claims about a subject. It does not model how an artifact was produced (specification §5.5).

edges.name: IETF SCITT architecture (RFC 9943)
edges.subject: typedstandards.org
edges.basis: An architecture for transparency services that register signed statements of any payload type and return receipts. That is the transparency layer Typed Standards fills with Sigstore Rekor today.

curation.reason: RFC 9943 confirmed at rfc-editor.org as the SCITT architecture (June 2026).

edges.name: SLSA Build Provenance v1.2
edges.subject: typedstandards.org
edges.basis: Build provenance for software artifacts, carried as an in-toto predicate. Typed Standards covers analytical artifacts instead (specification §5.5).

edges.name: Nanopublication Guidelines
edges.subject: typedstandards.org
edges.basis: Nanopublications are RDF named graphs that pair an atomic assertion with its provenance and publication information. Typed Standards is envelope-first JSON with capture-method labels, and consuming one as the other is not built (specification §5.5).

edges.name: Open Verification: the Proof-of-Control Standard for Agents
edges.publisher: Advanced AI Society (steward), in the LFDT-ProofOfControl GitHub organization
edges.subject: typedstandards.org
edges.basis: Specifies audit requirements and an evidence-token format (JWT and CWT) for an agent's runtime control: the data it touched, the authority it used, the tools it invoked. It points to SLSA and in-toto for artifact provenance and defines no record of how an analytical artifact was produced.

curation.reason: The seed described a v0.1 working draft; the pinned document states v1.0, a working draft for public comment.

edges.name: The Proof of Insight Protocol
edges.subject: typedstandards.org
edges.basis: Specifies the same kind of object as Typed Standards: a signed, content-addressed record of how an analysis was produced, as a graph of observe, compute, reason and attest steps, with a Sigstore Rekor profile. It is working draft v0.7.0, and neither depends on the other.

edges.name: Project NANDA AgentFacts
edges.subject: typedstandards.org
edges.basis: A JSON Schema for agent metadata (identity, endpoints, capabilities, evaluations, certification), used for discovery and routing. It defines no record of how an output was produced.

edges.name: MCP SEP-3094: Granular Citations Format (draft)
edges.subject: typedstandards.org
edges.basis: Proposes that MCP tool results carry citations to source fragments. Its content-integrity section says the proposal 'punts on a decision to add integrity checks', which a signed record provides at another layer.

edges.name: ATProto Lexicon
edges.subject: typedstandards.org
edges.basis: A schema language for typed records in the AT Protocol. The SciOS paper names it as a model for its common schema. Neither depends on the other.

edges.name: Open Knowledge Format v0.2
edges.subject: typedstandards.org
edges.basis: Organisational knowledge as Markdown files with YAML front matter, with provenance and attested-computation fields that are not signed. A raw-bytes/v1 record can sign such a file byte for byte, as this example signs core.md. The SciOS paper names it as a model for its schema.

edges.name: W3C DCAT 3
edges.subject: typedstandards.org
edges.basis: DCAT describes datasets and catalogs for discovery. A record's data-source references may cite DCAT-described datasets (specification §5.5).

curation.reason: Moved from Ring 1. The specification calls DCAT a different layer (§5.5), so the relation is complements, not builds-on.

edges.name: RO-Crate 1.3
edges.subject: typedstandards.org
edges.basis: A JSON-LD packaging format for research data. The specification names an RO-Crate compatibility profile as the direction for a multi-file package (open question Q1). Nothing is built.

curation.reason: Moved from Ring 1, where it was listed with WRROC. It is a direction under an open question, not something the specification builds on. Split from WRROC because the two are separate specifications.

edges.name: Workflow Run RO-Crate 0.6
edges.subject: typedstandards.org
edges.basis: RO-Crate profiles for recording tool and workflow executions. The specification names WRROC with RO-Crate as the direction for a multi-file package. Nothing is built.

curation.reason: Moved from Ring 1 and split from RO-Crate, for the same reasons.

edges.name: MIRA schema (draft)
edges.subject: typedstandards.org
edges.basis: A draft LinkML schema for question, claim and evidence graphs over research papers, built on Discourse Graphs and PROV. It signs nothing.

curation.reason: Listed at scios.tech/thoughts (read 2026-09-22) as a published schema. It builds on Discourse Graphs, as the specification does.

edges.name: civicaitools.org
edges.subject: civicaitools.org
edges.basis: The reference publishing application. It answers questions over civic open data through MCP servers and packages each published analysis as a signed record package.

curation.reason: Listed with socrata-mcp-server in the seed, and split from it because the two relate to the specification differently.

edges.name: socrata-mcp-server
edges.subject: github.com/npstorey/socrata-mcp-server
edges.basis: An MCP server that gives AI tools query access to Socrata open-data portals. It serves the tool results an analysis cites, and signs nothing itself.

edges.name: typedstandards.org verifier
edges.subject: typedstandards.org/verify
edges.basis: The site's client-side verifier runs verify-core's checks on a record package in the browser.

edges.name: typedstandards-eval-run-example
edges.subject: github.com/npstorey/typedstandards-eval-run-example
edges.basis: Turns one public AI benchmark evaluation run into two signed record packages that verify offline with one command (hub ADR-0028).

edges.name: qsv
edges.subject: github.com/dathere/qsv
edges.basis: An open issue on the project's own tracker, titled with the intent, and a plan comment posted from the maintainer account describe emitting JCS envelopes and Ed25519ph signatures for the Data Schematic output. The issue is open and labelled revisit-later.

statedIn.quote: Data Schematic: Replace Provenance free-text info with TypedStandards cryptographic signature
Phase 2 (signing) — Ed25519ph via --sign-key; signature envelope embedded in the HTML + sidecar
Revisit once TypedStandards supports something like Decentralized Identifiers

curation.reason: The one Ring 3 intent stated on the project's own public record.

edges.name: Verikan
edges.subject: github.com/dathere/Verikan
edges.basis: Its README at the pinned release lists a module that builds 'Typed Standards evidence packages' and states 'Evidence format by Typed Standards'. Its package builder targets the datHere content profile at specification revision v0.1.7.

curation.reason: Found by searching the qsv publisher's public repositories for the specification's name. Its own source states the relation.

edges.name: MCP for CKAN (okfn/mcp-server)
edges.subject: typedstandards.org
edges.basis: An MCP server for CKAN portals, in an early research phase, whose repository states the aim of making AI-generated answers traceable to their underlying datasets. It states no intent to produce signed records.

edges.name: hi-oss-ai-red-teaming
edges.subject: typedstandards.org
edges.basis: A platform for human red-teaming evaluations of AI systems that keeps reviewable records (conversation capture, reviewer verdicts, an append-only audit trail). None is signed, and its public text states no intent to produce signed evaluation records, so no evaluator relation is asserted.

edges.name: Strands Agents (Python SDK)
edges.subject: typedstandards.org
edges.basis: An agent SDK that runs the model and tool calls a producer records in queries[] and trace. Its README states nothing about provenance or signing.

edges.name: Microsoft Agent Framework
edges.subject: typedstandards.org
edges.basis: An agent and workflow framework with built-in OpenTelemetry tracing, the trace shape a record's trace field carries. Its README states nothing about signed records.

edges.name: Open-source AI foundation layer (Mila and Mozilla initiative)
edges.subject: typedstandards.org
edges.basis: An announced open standard of interface contracts, with a self-hosted reference implementation for running AI systems. Nothing is published yet, and the announcement says nothing about provenance or signing.

edges.name: Sigstore Rekor (hashedrekord)
edges.subject: typedstandards.org
edges.basis: A record package SHOULD carry a Sigstore Rekor inclusion proof, and the reference implementation uses Rekor's hashedrekord v0.0.1 entry type. verify-core checks Merkle inclusion against a pinned Rekor log key (specification §8.3.2, §9.2 check #8). This example's records carry no Rekor entry.

curation.reason: Restates map/edges/sigstore-rekor.yaml, which said records submit hashedrekord entries. The specification says a package SHOULD carry a Rekor proof (§8.3.2).

edges.name: RFC 3161 Time-Stamp Protocol
edges.subject: typedstandards.org
edges.basis: A record package SHOULD carry an RFC 3161 timestamp token from a public TSA (specification §8.3.2). When one is supplied, verify-core checks it against pinned TSA root anchors (§9.2 check #7). This example's records carry none.

curation.reason: Restates map/edges/rfc-3161.yaml, which said records carry RFC 3161 tokens. The specification says a package SHOULD carry one (§8.3.2).

edges.name: RFC 8032 EdDSA (Ed25519ph)
edges.subject: typedstandards.org
edges.basis: Every record signature is Ed25519ph, defined in RFC 8032 §5.1 (specification §8.3.1).

curation.reason: The signature algorithm of every record. Restates map/edges/rfc-8032.yaml, whose curation note counted this example's records as two.

edges.name: The did:key Method v0.9
edges.subject: typedstandards.org
edges.basis: A self-certifying signer's identifier is a did:key in base58btc form, derived from the signing key (specification §8.5.1, hub ADR-0030). One such identifier signs every record in this example.

curation.reason: Restates map/edges/did-key.yaml, which counted this example's records as two.

edges.name: Discourse Graphs
edges.subject: typedstandards.org
edges.basis: Discourse Graphs is a content-representation pattern, and Typed Standards wraps claim, question and evidence content in signed envelopes (specification Appendix C). The specification adopts those content types and the support, opposition and answer relations (§5.5, §7.5), and lists Discourse Graphs as an informative reference (§14.2). The content types are reserved by name only, and the current schema file names its relations differently.

curation.reason: Moved from Ring 1 and relabelled complements. Restates map/edges/discourse-graphs.yaml: the specification lists Discourse Graphs as an informative reference (§14.2) and reserves the pattern's content types by name only (§7.4).

edges.name: Nanopublication Guidelines
edges.subject: typedstandards.org
edges.basis: Nanopublications are RDF named graphs that pair an assertion with its provenance and publication information. Typed Standards is envelope-first JSON with capture-method labels, and the specification calls consuming Typed Standards content as nanopublications a plausible bridge but a separate effort (§5.5).

curation.reason: Restates map/edges/nanopublications.yaml. Its basis called the assertion atomic, which the pinned guidelines do not, and said consuming one as the other is not built, where the specification calls one direction a separate effort.

edges.name: Open Verification: the Proof-of-Control Standard for Agents
edges.publisher: Advanced AI Society (steward), in the LFDT-ProofOfControl GitHub organization
edges.subject: typedstandards.org
edges.basis: A working-draft standard for agents, v1.0. Its pinned frontispiece names the normative core as definitions, six domains, evidence properties, Verifiability Tiers, a binary threshold and conformance requirements, and lists a schema, test vectors and an audit checklist. It says nothing about Typed Standards or about records of how an analysis was produced.

curation.reason: Restates map/edges/proof-of-control.yaml from the pinned frontispiece alone, which shows neither an evidence-token format nor a pointer to SLSA or in-toto. Relabelled adjacent.

edges.name: Project NANDA AgentFacts
edges.subject: typedstandards.org
edges.basis: A JSON Schema for describing AI agents on the web: identity, endpoints including a dynamic routing endpoint, capabilities, evaluations and certification. It defines no record of how an output was produced.

curation.reason: Restates map/edges/nanda-agentfacts.yaml, whose basis said the schema is used for discovery. The pinned file has routing fields but does not mention discovery.

edges.name: ATProto Lexicon
edges.subject: typedstandards.org
edges.basis: A schema language for typed records in the AT Protocol. The SciOS paper likens its common schema to an ATProto Lexicon. Neither depends on the other.

curation.reason: Restates map/edges/atproto-lexicon.yaml, which said the paper names Lexicon as a model. The paper says its schema is akin to one.

edges.name: Open Knowledge Format v0.2
edges.subject: typedstandards.org
edges.basis: Knowledge about data and systems as Markdown files with YAML front matter, with provenance and attested-computation fields that are not signed. A raw-bytes/v1 record can sign such a file byte for byte when a program computed it from pinned inputs, as this example signs core.md. The SciOS paper likens its common schema to Google's Open Knowledge Format.

curation.reason: Restates map/edges/google-okf.yaml. The paper likens its schema to OKF rather than naming it a model, and the specification admits raw-bytes/v1 only for program-computed content (§8.2).

edges.name: MIRA schema
edges.subject: typedstandards.org
edges.basis: A schema for question, claim and evidence graphs in research, which links evidence to studies and to source documents such as papers, with one range marked provisional. It imports Discourse Graphs and PROV. It signs nothing.

curation.reason: Listed at scios.tech/thoughts (read 2026-09-22) as a published schema. Restates map/edges/mira-schema.yaml, whose name and basis called it a draft and LinkML; the pinned file says neither.

edges.name: qsv
edges.subject: github.com/dathere/qsv
edges.basis: Its README at tag 23.0.1 documents commands that write text files from CSV input: schema writes a JSON Schema file, and sniff, sortcheck and validate write JSON with their JSON options. Commands with randomized output take a --seed option "for reproducibility". The README names no Typed Standards record, and the signing it describes covers its prebuilt binary archives (zipsign).

curation.reason: Restates map/edges/qsv.yaml from the pinned README alone. That edge's could-emit relation rested on an issue thread that is not pinned.

edges.name: Verikan
edges.subject: github.com/dathere/Verikan
edges.basis: Its README at the pinned release lists a module, evidence.py, annotated "Typed Standards evidence packages", and states "Evidence format by Typed Standards".

curation.reason: Found by searching the qsv publisher's public repositories for the specification's name. Restates map/edges/verikan.yaml, whose basis named a specification revision the pinned README does not.

edges.name: Simple MCP Server (okfn/mcp-server)
edges.subject: typedstandards.org
edges.basis: An MCP server in an early research phase, for building AI data applications "with focus on traceability". Its structured tool output requires a sources field pointing to the original source of the data. The README says nothing about signed records.

curation.reason: Restates map/edges/okfn-ckan-mcp.yaml, whose name and basis said CKAN. The pinned README does not.
